Authentic Indian Taste in Phu Quoc – A Must Visit!
Oct 2025 • Couples
We had read many positive reviews about Maharaja Lounge before our visit to Phu Quoc, Vietnam, and our experience truly lived up to the expectations. We visited in the afternoon when it was pleasantly quiet and had the chance to meet the owner couple, both extremely warm and welcoming.

We ordered a few Indian dishes and were delighted with the flavors. The food tasted just like authentic, home-cooked Indian meals — fresh, delicious, and perfectly spiced. The service was quick, and the staff were courteous and attentive.

We were especially happy to know that it’s a 100% vegetarian restaurant, so there’s no concern about cross-contamination. The variety on the menu and the flexibility in spice levels make it appealing not just for Indians but also for anyone interested in genuine Indian cuisine.

Overall, we were very satisfied and would strongly recommend Maharaja Lounge to all food lovers visiting Phu Quoc.

Brilliant food we went twice
Apr 2025 • Family
The food here was definitely traditional indian food and tasted amazing. It took around 40mins to come out but it was so worth it as you can the chefs prepare it fresh. What i also really liked is how they bring a little bit for you to sample to see if the spice or salt etc is all fine, that's such a personised touch i havent seen before. The naans are a really good size and they have a good selection of food, albeit some was on the menu but when we asked it wasnt all available. Pizza pockets were a great snack, we also ordered the aloo gobi and vegan butter chicken. The owner also came round and asked each table how their food was and ate in the restaurant with the other diners which i thought was also another great touch 

The food was faultless as mentioned however one thing that let the place down was the service. Its very odd to have to go up to a desk to order your own food and then a number to be called in a train style way to then go to the back and carry your own trays of food to the table, this seems very odd and lacks the part of coming to a restaurant. Also the staff, the woman on the main desk is not friendly or smiley at all at greeting customers. 

The next morning we went at 11am for the indian breakfast but most things were sold out. The door also said they were still closed so we were going to walk straight past , its only when we looked in we saw customers and assumed it was open. There was no peaceful music playing like the evening before, there was no a.c or fan on, we had to ask for this to be put on. It was a bit of a let down from the night before. One of the workers was just standing at the back of the room but im not sure why as people collect their own food anyway when really she shouldve been clearing the plates which we had to keep asking her to do.

Overal brilliant for food, let down the staff serving and the idea of going up to order and collect your own food
